title: Stability and Nonlinear Dynamics of Field-Driven Extended Domain Walls with Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction
authors: Enzo Fabrizio Pusiol, Alberto Rosso, Alejandro B. Kolton
abstract: We analyze the stability and non-linear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) driven by an external magnetic field in the clean limit (i.e., in the absence of disorder and thermal fluctuations). We show that for moderate DMI strengths, the dynamics in both the low- and high-field regimes are accurately described by a rigid-wall Walker model that neglects flexural degrees of freedom. At intermediate fields, however, the system undergoes a transition into a non-trivial spatio-temporally chaotic regime characterized by dynamically roughened domain walls displaying single- or multi-valued profiles. The phase boundaries delimiting this regime in the magnetic field-DMI phase space are computed using a linear stability analysis based on Floquet theory applied to the extended domain wall, explicitly accounting for DMI and internal phase dynamics. Our theoretical analysis and predicted phase diagram are fully supported by numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the full Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
summary: This work analyzes how extended magnetic domain walls behave under external fields when DMI is present. It predicts a transition from simple, predictable dynamics to a complex, chaotic regime at intermediate fields. The findings map out a comprehensive phase diagram detailing these distinct dynamical states.
main_problem: The study investigates the stability and nonlinear dynamics of extended domain walls (DWs) subjected to an external magnetic field, incorporating the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya Interaction (DMI).
main_result: The system exhibits distinct dynamical regimes, transitioning from a rigid-wall Walker model to a non-trivial, spatio-temporally chaotic regime at intermediate fields, before re-stabilizing at high fields.
method: The analysis combines linear stability theory using Floquet analysis with numerical micromagnetic simulations solving the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation.
model_or_system: The system models extended domain walls in ultrathin magnetic heterostructures, governed by the LLG equation and an energy functional including Zeeman, exchange, magnetostatic, PMA, and DMI terms.
key_observables: DW velocity, interface width, multivalued fraction, and the internal magnetization angle ($\phi$).
important_parameters: External magnetic field ($B_z$ or $h$), DMI strength ($\delta$), and damping constant ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The initial analysis often assumes the 'clean limit' (no disorder/thermal fluctuations), and approximations include neglecting flexural degrees of freedom in certain regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the DW interface, the evolution of width and multivalued fraction across different field regimes, and the phase diagram mapping out stable and chaotic dynamical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the governing equations and basic dynamics (Walker model) to performing linear stability analyses (Floquet theory) to map out the phase diagram, culminating in the description of the chaotic transition regime.
why_interesting: The study of pattern formation and dynamic instabilities in magnetic systems provides analogies to complex dynamics seen in driven-dissipative quantum systems, particularly concerning phase transitions between ordered and chaotic states.
